ai.title: Terminal PTY spawn fallback to childprocess
ai.summary: Wrapped `bunPty.spawn` in try/catch in `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts`. If PTY creation throws, logs error with platform/arch and falls back to `child_process` logic. Prevents crash on unsupported PTY environments.

eli5.text: When you open a built-in terminal inside the app, the system first tries to create it with the preferred PTY method (which gives the best experience). If that preferred method fails on your computer, the app now catches the error, quietly switches to the standard child process method instead, and keeps working instead of crashing. You might notice nothing if your computer supports the preferred method, but on unsupported setups the terminal still loads and works, just using the fallback approach. This is a stability fix, so no action is needed from you.

ai.title: Version 1.0.340
ai.summary: Release package version bumped to 1.0.340. Internal versioning update in npm-app/release/package.json.

eli5.text: The release number for the AI coding tool was updated, which is mostly a behind-the-scenes labeling change so installs stay current. Updating to this version is what gets you the latest improvements that shipped with it, including an upgraded evaluations view that now shows a turns-per-case metric alongside score and duration, enlarged model logos, and display name mapping. There is a separate database change in this batch that removes a required provider constraint on the sync failure table, though that is not user-facing. No action is required on your part for the version bump, but installing it will bring in those interface and data-model updates.

ai.title: Lazy load bun-pty native module
ai.summary: Refactored `bun-pty` loading in `npm-app/src/native/pty.ts` to be asynchronous and lazy via `loadBunPty()`. Prevents startup crashes when native libraries are missing or platform unsupported by deferring errors. Callers in `cli.ts`, `index.ts`, and `terminal/base.ts` updated to `await` shell creation and reset functions.

eli5.text: When the app starts up, it no longer tries to load a special program (used for running terminal commands) right away. Instead, it waits until that program is actually needed, so if the program can't load or isn't supported on the current system, the app won't crash on startup. The parts of the app that use this program now wait for it to load before they try to use it, making the startup process more stable.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.341
ai.summary: Internal version increment for the codebuff package to 1.0.341. Updates the version field in npm-app/release/package.json. No functional changes or user-facing features included in this release.

eli5.text: The software you’re using got a new internal version number today, but nothing about how it works changed for you. That number just marks a bundle of behind-the-scenes work that shipped together, the most noticeable piece being a tweak so the terminal window feature only loads some of its support pieces when they’re actually needed instead of every time. If you open the app now, things will start a little faster on machines where you never use that terminal feature, and it should still connect to your terminal programs through a backup method if the main path ever has trouble. No buttons moved and no menus changed, so you wouldn’t see a difference unless you were watching how the app starts up.

ai.title: Pricing credit estimate reduced to few hours
ai.summary: Updated the `DEFAULT_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT` description in `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` from 'a day of intense coding' to 'a few hours'. This aligns the marketing copy with actual usage patterns. Scope limited to the web pricing page.

eli5.text: The free-trial credit estimate shown on the pricing page was shortened. Instead of saying the credits will last a full day of intense coding, the text now says they will only cover a few hours of work. If you looked at the pricing page today, you would see the wording now reflects a more realistic short window for new users experimenting with the assistant. This is a live text change on the public pricing page.

ai.title: Add console output suppression utility
ai.summary: New `suppressConsoleOutput` utility in `npm-app/src/utils/suppress-console.ts` wraps `console.error`, `console.warn`, and `console.log` to filter specific messages. `npm-app/src/native/pty.ts` uses this to hide `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` errors during `bun-pty` dynamic import, while `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` refactors PostHog error suppression to use the shared utility. The implementation supports multiple concurrent suppression filters per method and provides cleanup functions to restore original console behavior.

eli5.text: The app now quietly hides certain confusing error messages that would normally pop up in the background when it tries to load a terminal feature, so you won't see scary crash-like text during startup. It also cleans up how unrelated noisy messages from an analytics tool are blocked, making the code easier to maintain. If you happened to be watching the background logs closely, you might notice fewer red error lines; otherwise, your day-to-day use looks exactly the same.

ai.title: Refactor CI release workflows for CodeCane
ai.summary: Split monolithic `release-binaries.yml` into modular `build.yml`, `prod.yml`, and `staging.yml` workflows. Added automated staging releases triggered by `[codecane]` PR titles, publishing to `codecane@beta`. Updated `npm-app/release-staging` package and build scripts to support dual-binary distribution.

eli5.text: When a developer opens a pull request to test the new CodeCane feature, you'll now get a pre-release version automatically published for testing on the beta channel, without needing a manual approval step. This was made possible by splitting the old monolithic release process into modular workflows, where the staging workflow checks for '[codecane]' in PR titles and triggers the appropriate build and release pipeline. If you're working with CodeCane during development, you can rely on fresh binaries being available in the beta channel right after submitting a PR with the right tag.

ai.title: CI release workflows reorganized with npm-app prefix
ai.summary: GitHub Actions release workflows renamed from `releases/` subdirectory to flat `npm-app-release-` prefix. `prod.yml` switched `version_type` input from freeform string to choice enum, replaced custom bash semver logic with `npm version`, and renamed jobs. `staging.yml` updated `uses` reference to new build workflow path. `npm-app/scripts/release.js` updated API dispatch URL and manual trigger instructions to match new workflow filenames.

eli5.text: If you trigger a production release of the app, you now pick the version bump type from a fixed list (patch, minor, or major) instead of typing it freely, and the assistant that runs the release process uses a standard tool to calculate the new version number instead of custom math. The helper script that starts a release now points to the renamed release-checklist location, so the link you'd open to run things by hand is different. This is live today for anyone running a production release.
